meta.case_type: Pricing Strategy, Competitive Response, Supply Chain

prompt.context: We are consulting for VoiceDirect. They have been packaging and reselling excess capacity on their cellular network to highly fragmented prepaid phone card buyers. Over the past year, VoiceDirect has lost significant market share.
prompt.question: What is happening, and how can VoiceDirect recover?

clarifying_info.a: Only three other players: Sprint, AT&T, and T-Mobile.

clarifying_info.q: What is VoiceDirect's pricing vs. competitors?
clarifying_info.a: VoiceDirect charges five cents per minute; all three competitors charge three cents per minute.

clarifying_info.q: What is the marginal cost of providing additional minutes?
Is there an existing contract with major prepay providers?
clarifying_info.a: No. Virgin Mobile already has an agreement with one of the competitors, and the rest of the market is very fragmented.

framework: Draw a market diagram: US cellular market splits into Contract (post-pay) and Prepaid segments; focus is on Prepaid excess-capacity resale
Quantify the price gap: VoiceDirect at $0.05/min vs. competitors at $0.03/min — calculate the percentage price premium

Establish why the premium may or may not be justified: (1) no differentiation exists, (2) differentiation exists but is not perceived, (3) differentiation exists and is perceived but the low-end segment is not willing to pay for it
Evaluate strategic options for each hypothesis: price match, marketing/bundling initiatives, vertical integration into prepay branding, renegotiating with repackagers
Assess cannibalization risk: if VoiceDirect's postpaid rate is above $0.03/min, cutting prepaid price must not bleed into the postpaid base
Quantify the demand impact of a price cut using price elasticity of demand

questions.prompt: Calculate VoiceDirect's percentage price premium over competitors.
questions.guidance: A strong answer sets up the formula (Price Premium % = (VoiceDirect price - competitor price) / competitor price), plugs in the numbers, and arrives at 66.7% (~66%). Candidate should note this is a substantial premium for a commodity-like product in a price-sensitive segment.

math.setup: Price premium % = (VoiceDirect price − Competitor price) / Competitor price

questions.prompt: What are the hypotheses for why VoiceDirect is losing market share, and what strategy follows from each?
questions.guidance: Three hypotheses: (1) No real differentiation — strategy: match price at $0.03/min; (2) Differentiation exists but is not perceived — strategy: marketing initiatives (joint campaigns with strong brands, bundle with a phone, two-for-one, supplemental postpaid cards, swap competitors' cards for VoiceDirect cards subject to regulatory check); (3) Differentiation exists and is perceived but low-end customers are unwilling to pay — strategy: also match price. For (1) and (3) the candidate must flag cannibalization risk if the postpaid rate is above $0.03/min.

questions.prompt: What other strategic options should VoiceDirect explore beyond pricing?
questions.guidance: (1) Contract with major prepay providers — ruled out because Virgin Mobile already has an exclusive with a competitor and the remaining market is too fragmented. (2) Vertical integration: create VoiceDirect's own prepay brand, repackaging minutes directly, unless Virgin's brand strength makes competition impractical. (3) Renegotiate with repackagers (gas stations, Walmart, etc.) to absorb the price delta rather than passing it to consumers — check whether the premium reaches the consumer level or is absorbed in the channel margin.

questions.prompt: Estimate the impact on demand of cutting the price from $0.05 to $0.03 per minute, given price elasticity of demand ε ≈ −1.25.
questions.guidance: Candidate should first explain what elasticity means (% change in quantity demanded divided by % change in price) and why it is negative (demand and price move in opposite directions). Then calculate % change in price and multiply by elasticity to get % change in demand.

math.setup: ε = (ΔDemand / Demand) / (ΔPrice / Price); ΔDemand% = ε × ΔPrice%

brainstorming.prompt: What marketing initiatives could VoiceDirect pursue if its differentiation exists but is not perceived by the market?

categories.name: Co-branding and partnerships
ideas: Joint campaigns with powerful consumer brands that offer prepaid cards (marginal cost is zero so incremental revenue is pure upside)
Offer prepaid cards bundled with a handset

categories.name: Promotions
ideas: Supplemental postpaid cards for existing contract customers
Exchange competitors' prepaid cards for VoiceDirect cards (subject to regulatory review)

categories.name: Channel
ideas: Increase shelf presence and visibility at repackagers (gas stations, Walmart, convenience stores)
Renegotiate repackager margins so consumer-facing price drops without reducing VoiceDirect's wholesale rate

recommendation: Immediately cut the prepaid resale price to at least the competitor level of $0.03 per minute
Assess whether VoiceDirect should vertically integrate into the prepay repackaging market, given that people with bad credit and those under 18 cannot sign contracts — this segment is growing
risks: Cannibalization of existing postpaid (contract) customer base if the new prepaid price undercuts the effective postpaid per-minute rate
Virgin Mobile's entrenched position may limit the attractiveness of building a proprietary prepay brand
next_steps: Verify the postpaid effective per-minute rate to quantify cannibalization risk before finalizing the price cut
Conduct a channel margin analysis to determine how much of the current price premium reaches consumers vs. is absorbed by repackagers
Explore regulatory feasibility of a card-swap promotion
Model the full revenue impact using the ~50% demand uplift estimate from elasticity analysis
